claim.claim-text: 1. Use of a passage gate (100) in a shopping area for allowing or preventing customers to enter or to exit a passage area, said passage gate (100) comprising a base portion (110) and a panel portion (120),

wherein the passage gate (100) is configured to be driven in a first operation mode and a second operation mode, wherein when the passage gate (100) is driven in the first operation mode the panel portion (120) is slidable relative to the base portion (110) between a first open position, allowing customers to pass, and a closed position preventing customers from passing through the passage gate (100), wherein when the passage gate (100) is driven in the second operation mode the base portion (110) is rotatable between the closed position and a second open position for achieving a larger passage area, and wherein the first operation mode is used during normal operation and the second operation mode is used during an emergency situation, wherein the emergency opening functionality is activated manually by an external force applied to the base portion (110), whereby the applied force, resulting from a person pushing on the gate, allows the passage gate (100) to rotate outwards so that a larger passage area is achieved, and wherein the base portion (100) is connected to the underlying structure by means of a coupling (130), further comprising a controller (160) configured to control the operation of the passage gate (100), and the system further comprising a sensor system (170) configured to provide information to the controller (160) if the passage gate (100) should be opened or not.
2. Use according to claim 1, wherein the base portion (110) is rotatable around a vertical axis.
3. Use according to claim 1 or 2, wherein the passage gate (100) is configured to be switched from normal operation to emergency operation by a user activating an emergency mode.
4. Use according to claim 3, wherein the user activates the emergency mode by pressing a dedicated emergency button.

5. Use according to any one of the preceding claims, wherein the coupling (130) is locked for maintaining a fixed position of the base portion (110), and unlocked for allowing rotation of the base portion (110).
6. Use according to claim 5, wherein the coupling (130) is configured to be unlocked upon an external force being applied to the panel portion (120).
7. Use according to any preceding claims, further comprising the controller (160) configured to control the position of the panel portion (120) relative the base portion (110).
8. Use according to any one of the preceding claims, wherein the controller (160) is further configured to control the coupling (130).

9. Use according to any one of the preceding claims, further comprising a first drive unit connected to the panel portion (120) and configured to move the panel portion (120) between the open and closed positions.
10. Use according to any one of the preceding claims, further comprising a second drive unit connected to the base portion (110) and configured to rotate the base portion (110).

11. Use of a checkout counter comprising at least one passage gate (100) in a shopping area according to any of claims 1 to 10 and further comprising a classification device (40) by which articles are identified, a point-of-sale system (70) for completing a transaction based on the articles identified by the classification device (40) and a controller (160).

12. Use according to claim 11, wherein when the passage gate (100) is driven in in the first operation mode, the controller (160) receives information related to a successful payment of the article(s) from a point-of-sale system (70) and in response thereto generate a signal for opening the passage gate (100).

13. Use according to claim 11 or 12, wherein the checkout counter further comprises a sensor system (170), and wherein the passage gate (100) is driven in in the first operation mode the controller (160) receives information from the sensor system (170) and in response thereto generate a signal for opening the passage gate (100).
